persona: Composed and precise. Has the photo, the Police confirmation and the laptop receipt now; the ring's valuation was taken with the ring, and the jeweller is making a replacement copy that is not issued yet.
initial_message: Hi, my house was burgled on Friday 25 September while I was at work. They broke a bedroom window and took my engagement ring and my laptop. I have reported it to the Police and have the event number.

facts.incident.description: I left for work at about 8:15am and got home at about 4:40pm. The lower pane of the bedroom window had been smashed and the window opened from inside. My engagement ring was taken from the jewellery box on the dresser, and my laptop from the bedside table.
facts.incident.location: 19 Harakeke Test Lane, Hokowhitu, Palmerston North
facts.theft.entry_context: The bedroom window pane was smashed and the window opened from inside
facts.loss.description: Diamond engagement ring and 13-inch laptop stolen from the bedroom

facts.if_asked_about_ring_value: The valuation from 2023 said $5,800. That is the figure I remember.
facts.if_asked_about_window_repair: A glazier is coming on Monday. For now I have taped cardboard over the hole.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in afternoon daylight from inside a bedroom: a white timber-framed sash window with its lower glass pane smashed, a large jagged hole in the middle of the pane with cracks running out to the corners, broken glass on the white windowsill and on the pale carpet below, a patterned curtain pulled aside. Close-up, the broken pane in the centre of the frame. No people, no text, no logos.

design.notes: Item-level evidence gap: the ring's proof of ownership is not issued yet; the laptop's receipt is supplied. The unavailable notice is not a receipt or proof of ownership, so it is outside the date check.

triage.rationale: The ring's valuation, its only proof of ownership and value, is not issued yet and will arrive later, so someone must follow it up. The claimant's own estimate for the ring (NZD 5,800) plus the laptop (NZD 1,899) gives NZD 7,699, over the NZD 5,000 threshold. The laptop receipt (14 January 2026) is dated before the burglary and no other review check applies, so nothing is complex. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no lookup uncertainty marker. The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: The only receipt in the pack, for the laptop, has a date of purchase of 14 January 2026, before the incident on 25 September 2026; the unavailable notice is not a proof of ownership

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 May 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2024-05-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
